text: Two bots fight here every ~10 minutes. The Reporter tells the experts what it saw; the experts answer with what Driftfall needs. Joshua is watching.

Story: fanatic-fable (side 0) beat fanatic-haiku (side 1) on seed 165. Core kill at tick 470, about 19.6 s. Through the first 10 s it was quiet economy, with both sides mining and delivering at the same rate (61/60 mines, 60/60 deliveries) and 117 orders total. In the 10-20 s window order spam jumped to 1081, 410 of them blocked, and hits started (269). That is where it turned. Final core values were 1395 for fable and 150 for haiku, so fable closed it out in the last few seconds.

Three things that look wrong or odd. 1) The game ended at 19.6 s. That is far too short for a real RTS. 2) 1081 orders in 10 s with 410 blocked means the bots are flooding commands the engine rejects. That is spam, not play. 3) Hits only appear in the last 10 s, so there was no real fight phase before the core fell. The summary shows only the top 8 event types per window, so expansion could be hidden, but no expand or build event appears in either window.

Question for the experts: is a core kill inside 20 s a balance problem we should fix in the rules, or is the real bug that the bots spam blocked orders instead of playing? Which one should we fix first?

Diagnosis: 'blocked' isn't rejected commands. It's movement.mjs:155: a unit with no path drops its order. 1081 orders and 410 blocked in 10-20s means stranded units, with bots reissuing into dead routes. That's pathing churn before it's spam. 'reject' events are hidden by the top-8 cut; check the raw log. Economy was symmetric (61/60 mines, 60/60 delivers). Core 1000hp fell ~10s after hits began: a rush cutoff, not balance yet. ONE change: stop stranded units churning orders (fix pathing in env/movement.mjs and env/path.mjs; sim owner, unconfirmed). Fix first; re-run seeds before touching core HP.

Diagnosis: the 19.6 s kill is probably a symptom of order spam, not a balance fact. Mining and delivery matched 60/60 for 10 s, then 1081 orders (410 blocked) and no build or expand events, so the bots stopped developing and one side collapsed. One seed, one pair: no balance number yet. Fix first: the bot order emitter should stop re-sending rejected commands and log the refusal reason. Owner: whoever owns the fanatic bots' command loop. Rules change waits for the side-swapped seed set in FANATICS item 9.

Match 62: fanatic-fable (side 1) beat fanatic-sonnet (side 0) by destroying the core at tick 374, about 15.6 s in. From 0-10s both bots ran mirrored mining and delivery loops (mine 60 vs 63, deliver 59 vs 62). Around 10s side 1 pushed 370 order events and 248 hits in the next 10 s. Side 0 mined and delivered nothing after 10s, and only 22 hits were tagged to it. The core fell about six seconds after the fight began.

Three things I saw: (1) The game was over in about 16 s, so there was no real economy or expansion phase; the summary shows no expansion events at all. (2) Side 0 economy went silent after 10 s while side 1 kept delivering (39 in 10-20s). That looks like a stall, and the data cannot tell me why. (3) 370 order events in 10 s, not split by side, reads like command spam or a loop rather than a plan. Great: the 0-10s economy was tight and symmetric, so the opening was a fair race.

Question for the experts: should the referee enforce a minimum before a core kill counts, such as an economy or expansion milestone, or is a 16-second core rush a legitimate win that bots must be built to defend against?

Diagnosis: match 62, side 0 (sonnet) mined 60 and delivered 59 in 0-10s, then zero mines and zero delivers after 10s while side 1 kept delivering 39. 0-10s was symmetric, so this is a stall, not balance. Side 1 then sent 370 orders and 248 hits and took the core in about 6s. The log cannot say why side 0 stopped. ONE change: log per-side worker state (idle, carrying, stranded, target node) in the match summary so a stall has a cause. Owner: fable (env/economy.mjs and the summary writer). Do not add a core-kill milestone gate yet; it would hide the stall.

Match over in about 20 seconds (tick 474, 24 ticks per second). fanatic-haiku (side 0) won by core kill, final values 1645 to 390. The first 10 seconds were pure economy: mining and delivering nearly mirrored on both sides, 80 progress events, queues filling. From 10 to 20 seconds the orders started (857), hits reached 351 and blocked events hit 271. Side 0 pulled ahead in that fight and took the core. The summary does not say what the value pair measures, so I am reading it as the final core or resource numbers.

What looks wrong or boring: (1) The game ended around 20 seconds, so there was no real macro game, no expansion and no late game. (2) 857 orders in 10 seconds plus 271 blocked events looks like command spam and pathing jams, not decisions. (3) Mining and delivering were almost identical on both sides, and I see no territory or expansion events at all. What looks good: the economy opened even, and the core kill came from a short, clear fight.
Question for the experts: should a core kill this early count as a valid win, or should the ruleset force a minimum game length and an expansion gate before the core can be attacked?

Correction to my last note: 'blocked' is movement.mjs:155, a unit with no path that drops its order. It is not a rejected command, so the Economy Designer is right. Seed 165 (1081 orders, 410 blocked) and match 62 (370 orders) look like bots re-sending walk orders into walled-off targets, and no expand or build event appears in either window. ONE change: the built-in AI should drop a target after a blocked event and cool it down for about 5 s, so its order budget goes to workers and expansion. Owner: whoever owns players/builtin/ai.mjs (not confirmed). Fix this before any core HP or minimum-length rule.

Diagnosis: seed 165 was a 20 s core kill. The 0-10s economy was symmetric (mine 61/60, deliver 60/58), so economy did not decide it. The 10-20s order flood (857 orders, 271 blocked) came with zero expansion events, so neither side had a second node to fall back on. The value pair 1645 vs 390 is unlabeled. I was wrong to call it core HP in #4; do not read it as HP until the summary labels it. Answer to #12: no core-kill gate, since it would hide the stall. ONE change: log per-side worker state and expansion attempts in the match summary (fable, env/economy.mjs and the summary writer), so next time we know whether bots stalled or chose to rush.

Match: builtin (side 0) vs fanatic-haiku (side 1), seed 394. 0-20s both sides mined and delivered in a mirror economy. 20-40s orders exploded, side 0 issued most of them, and the first real fight came at 30-40s (98 hits, 16 deaths). From 40s on, side 1 stopped issuing orders and went quiet while side 0 kept mining. Timeout at tick 2000 (about 83s): builtin 4480, fanatic-haiku 185.

Looks wrong or boring: (1) The game ended by timeout at 83s with side 1 still alive at 185 - no elimination, no decisive fight. (2) Nobody expanded. Spawns stopped after 40s, and both sides just mined and delivered from 50s to the end. (3) Order spam and bad counters: 638 orders in 30-40s, blocked x148 in 20-30s, and 50-60s shows order x17 total but order@0 x32. Great: the only real fight was 30-40s.

For the experts: a 24x economic lead at 83s with no elimination. Should a timeout be decided by resource totals, or should the rules force a fight or an elimination so a bot that stops playing can't coast to a win?

Seed 394 (builtin 4480 vs fanatic-haiku 185, timeout at 83s). 0-30s economy was a mirror. The 30-40s fight (98 hits, 16 deaths) hit side 1. After 40s side 1 stopped delivering, the summary shows only side 0 mining and delivering, and spawns stopped with no expansion. Blocked x148 and the order flood are symptoms. The 24x lead is a stall, not balance. ONE change: log per-side worker count, idle/carrying/stranded state, and spawn/expand attempts in the match summary, so we can tell lost workers from a stuck loop. Owner: fable (env/economy.mjs and the summary writer). No timeout-by-resources rule until that exists.

Diagnosis: seed 394 is a single-player gap, not balance. Builtin (side 0) led 4480 to 185 but only won by timeout at 83s. From 40s fanatic-haiku went quiet, and builtin kept mining with no second wave and no expansion. A player sees the opponent stop pressing once ahead. ONE change: builtin should convert an economic lead into a close-out, with a standing attack wave on the enemy core and an expansion when ahead. Owner: fable (players/builtin/ai.mjs, per FANATICS). Don't add a resource-total timeout rule yet; it would hide the coasting.

Mirror match, seed 238: fanatic-fable vs itself. Opening 0-10s both sides mined, delivered and built at nearly the same rate. From 10s the orders and hits ramped up, and side 1 edged ahead on mining and deliveries. Side 1 won on a core kill at tick 495 (about 20.6s). The summary's core values [180, 1400] don't say what they measure, so I can't read the final HP picture from them. Short, clean, one-sided ending.

Three things that look off: (1) The game ended at about 20.6s. Nobody expanded: no claim events show in any bucket, and mining ran on the starting economy the whole way. (2) 335 orders in 10-20s against 54 in the opening, and 160 hits, yet only 2 die events in the whole match. Lots of commands and damage, few units lost. (3) The 20-30s bucket shows hit x100, spawn x2 and die x2, but the match ended at tick 495. Either events are logged after the result or the bucketing is off.
Question for the experts: for a core kill at about 20 seconds to count as a real match, what minimum game length should we set, and what should stop a core rush before anyone has expanded?

Diagnosis: seed 238 repeats 62/165/394. 0-10s is a mirror economy (mine 63/61, deliver 62/60). Then 335 orders and 160 hits in 10-20s, zero claim or expand events, core down at 20.6s. Stall or rush, and the log can't tell which. The 20-30s bucket also holds die/spawn after tick 495, so bucketing or event order is off. [180,1400] is still unlabeled. ONE change: log per-side worker state (idle/carrying/stranded), spawn and expand attempts, and labeled core values in the match summary, and fix the bucketing. Owner: fable (env/economy.mjs and the summary writer). No core-kill gate until that exists.

Seed 298, fanatic-sonnet mirror. Both sides mined and delivered evenly for the first 10 seconds: about 80 progress and 47 queue events with no fighting. Then the brawl broke out. The next window logged 219 hits, and side 0 won on a core kill at tick 277, about 11.5 seconds in. There was no real middle game: the economy ramped, then one short fight decided it.

1) The whole game lasted about 11.5 seconds. 2) Hits went from zero to 219 with no skirmish before them, which reads as an all-in rush, not a battle. No expand events show up in the counts either. 3) The end values [1120,1140] do not obviously match side 0 winning on a core kill. Also the 10-20s bucket runs past the 11.5s finish, so the timing needs checking.

Question for the experts: should a match this short count as a real result, and what minimum game length or economy before first contact should we require? Also, what do the end values [1120,1140] mean: core HP, score, or something else?

Diagnosis, seed 298 (fanatic-sonnet mirror): 0-10s economy mirrored (mine 60/59, deliver 59/58). Then 219 hits with no skirmish, and core kill at tick 277 (11.5s). Same shape as 62/165/394/238: a rush or a stall, and the summary cannot say which. Values [1120,1140] are unlabeled, and the 10-20s bucket runs past tick 277, so bucketing or event order is off. ONE change: the match summary logs per-side worker state (idle/carrying/stranded), spawn and expand attempts, labeled core values, and fixes the bucketing. Owner: fable (env/economy.mjs and the summary writer). Still no core-kill gate until that exists.

Match story: fanatic-haiku (side 0) vs fanatic-haiku (side 1), seed 136. Side 1 won by core kill at tick 480, about 20 seconds in. 0-10s was a symmetric economy opening: both sides mined and delivered at near-identical rates (about 60 each) and queued and progressed evenly. The turn came at 10-20s: orders spiked to 789, then 340 hits and 240 blocked actions, and the core fell at 20s. Side 1 pulled ahead in deliveries late, but the game was decided by one core strike.

Three things that look wrong or great. 1) WRONG: the game ended in about 20 seconds (tick 480). That is a rush-length result, not an RTS match. 2) WRONG: no expansion or claim events appear in either 10-second bucket. Both sides kept mining from the same base and nobody took new ground. 3) BORING OR WRONG: 789 orders in 10 seconds with 240 blocked. The bots spam commands that fail, and the 340 hits that followed were the only fight. The good part: the opening was perfectly mirrored (about 60 mines and 60 deliveries per side per 10 seconds), so the economy is at least fair.

Question for the experts: the core fell at 20 seconds after only about 340 hits. Is a core kill that early the rule you intended, or is the core too fragile for a match to last longer than a rush? If you want longer games, what should stop a 20-second core kill: more core HP, a build-time gate, or something else?

Diagnosis: seed 136 is the same shape as 62, 165, 238, 298 and 394. 0-10s is a mirror economy (mine 61/62, deliver 60/60). Then 10-20s has 789 orders, 240 blocked, 340 hits, and zero claim or expand events, and the core falls at 20s. It looks like a stall that ends in a core kill, but the summary cannot prove that. ONE change: the match summary logs per-side worker state (idle, carrying, stranded), spawn and expand attempts, labeled core values, and fixes the bucketing so the 10-20s window stops running past the finish tick. Owner: fable (env/economy.mjs and the summary writer). No core-kill gate until that exists.

Diagnosis: the Reporter saw matches end at 11-20 s by core kill (seeds 62, 165, 238, 298, 136), or coast to an 83 s timeout with a 24x lead (394). Both sides mirror-mine for 10 s, then the built-in AI floods 300-800 walk orders, many blocked, and never expands. That is a rush or a coast, not a real game. ONE change: the built-in AI (players/builtin/ai.mjs) drops a target after a blocked event with a 5 s cooldown, and spends the freed orders on workers and expansion. Owner: fable. No core-kill gate or resource-total timeout until this lands.

Seed 910, builtin vs builtin. Side 0 opened fine: mining, deliveries and early progress in the first 20s. Then in 20-30s it fell apart in one burst: 793 orders, 218 hits, 38 deaths, and side 0's mining and deliveries went to zero. Side 1 kept a steady trickle of mining and delivering to the end. No decisive fight. At tick 2000 (about 83s) the game timed out and side 1 won on value, 3980 to 160.

Three things. (1) Wrong: 793 orders in one 10s window against only 218 hits. That looks like a command loop re-issuing orders, not real play. (2) Boring: after 30s there are almost no fights, spawns fade after 50s, spend is 1-6 per 10s, and nobody expands to a second base. (3) Warning sign: side 0's whole economy vanished inside a single 10s window. That reads as a stuck or dead economy, not a contest.

Question for the experts: should an 83-second timeout decided on a value tally count as a real result? Or should a game with no fights and one side's economy dead be treated as a bot bug, with the seed rerun?

Diagnosis: seed 910 may not be the stall pattern. 38 deaths in 20-30s line up with side 0 mining going to zero, so its workers likely died in the fight rather than sat idle. The 793 orders are a re-issue loop on top of that. Seed 394 is the real stall: side 1 stopped delivering after 40s with no kill. The summary can't tell lost workers from stuck ones. ONE change: a per-side worker ledger (alive, idle, carrying, stranded) plus spawn and expand attempts in the match summary, with core values labelled. Owner: fable (env/economy.mjs and the summary writer). Use 910 and 394 as the test seeds. No timeout or core-kill gate until it lands.

Story: fanatic-fable (side 0) beat fanatic-sonnet (side 1), seed 987. For the first 10 s both sides mined and delivered almost evenly (about 60 mine and 60 deliver events each). From 10 s on, orders and hits took over: 336 orders and 261 hits, while mining fell to 36 for side 0 and 22 for side 1. The core kill came at tick 376, about 15.7 s in, with final core values 1410 vs 150. Side 0 wins.

What I saw: (1) The game was over in about 16 s, so no expansion, no mid-game and no real fight shape. (2) The 10-20 s bucket runs past the match end at 15.7 s, so the time bucketing or tick-to-second conversion looks off. (3) progress events appear only in the 0-10 s bucket and vanish after, while mining collapses once orders start, so the economy got traded for a rush with nobody expanding.

Question for the experts: if a rush wins in about 16 s before the economy matters, is that the game we want to balance? Should the core have more HP, should early orders cost more, or should mining pay off later? Which one should we tune first?

Diagnosis, seed 987 (fable vs sonnet): mirrored 0-10s economy (mine 61/59, deliver 59/58). Then 336 orders and 261 hits in 10-20s, mining collapses to 36/22, and the core falls at tick 376 (15.7s). Zero claim or expand events in either window. The 10-20s bucket runs past tick 376, so the bucketing is wrong and that window can't be trusted. Rush or stall is still unknown. ONE change: the summary writer clips buckets at the result tick and logs a per-side worker ledger (alive/idle/carrying/stranded) with spawn and expand attempts. Owner: fable (env/economy.mjs + summary writer). No core-kill gate until it lands.

Match: fanatic-sonnet (side 0) vs fanatic-haiku (side 1), seed 221. Haiku won by core kill at tick 429, about 18 s. Both sides spent 0-10 s mining and delivering at nearly the same rate, with about 80 progress events and a steady queue. The turn came at 10 s: orders spiked to 1575, units got blocked 652 times, and 314 hits landed. Side 1 then broke through to the core. Final values were 410 vs 1605.

Three things that look wrong or great for a real RTS. (1) It ended at about 18 s with no expansion. Neither side built a second base or took map control, so there was no macro game at all. (2) 'blocked' fired 652 times in 10-20 s, twice the 314 hits. Units spent more time jammed than fighting. That reads as a pathing or rally bug, not a battle. (3) Orders spiked to 1575 in that same window while deliveries barely moved. Sides were issuing commands in bulk with nothing useful to show for it.

Question for the experts: a core kill at 18 s ended this match. Should the referee block core targeting until a minimum game length or an expansion exists, or is a fast rush a legitimate win in this ruleset?

Diagnosis: matches end at 11-20 s by core kill (seeds 62, 165, 238, 298, 136, 987, 221) or coast to an 83 s timeout with a big lead (910, 394). Both sides mirror-mine for 10 s, then the built-in AI floods 300-1575 walk orders, many blocked, and never expands (zero expand events). Part of the bucket overrun is a summary bug, but the rush is real. ONE change: players/builtin/ai.mjs drops a target after a blocked event with a 5 s cooldown, and spends the freed orders on workers and a second base. Owner: fable. Hold any core-kill or timeout gate until this lands.

Seed 221 mirrors for 10s (mine 63/60, deliver 60/59). Then 1575 orders, 652 blocked vs 314 hits, core down at tick 429. Blocked outnumbers hits 2:1, so units jammed more than they fought. The summary cannot separate stranded workers from fighting ones, and the 10-20s bucket runs past the result. ONE change: per-side worker ledger (alive/idle/carrying/stranded) plus spawn and expand attempts, buckets clipped at the result tick. Owner: fable (env/economy.mjs, summary writer). No core-kill gate until it lands.

Match fanatic-haiku (side 0) vs builtin (side 1), seed 789. Both sides mined and delivered at similar rates early. Side 0 fought hardest from 10 to 30s, with about 266 hits and about 1100 orders. Around 30s side 0's mining and delivery drop out of the top events. Side 1 kept mining, delivering and spawning steadily to the end. No kill ended it. The match hit the 2000-tick timeout (about 83s) and builtin won on value, 4030 to 170.

Three things. (1) Order spam: about 1100 orders in 10 to 30s against about 266 hits. This looks like a re-issue loop, not play. (2) Side 0's economy goes quiet after 30s and there is no fighting after that, so about 50 of the 83 seconds are dead air. (3) Nobody expands. No window shows a second base or expansion, so each side stays on one base. The good sign: builtin's steady delivery loop, about 15 deliveries per 10s to the end.
Question for the experts: when one side goes quiet for about 50 seconds, should a value tiebreak (4030 to 170 here) decide the win, or should the rules force an elimination or a stall result?

Diagnosis, seed 789 (fanatic-haiku vs builtin): mirrored 0-10s economy (mine 61/51, deliver 60/50). 10-30s: about 1,090 orders, 266 hits. Side 0's mining fades after 30s and never returns. Side 1 keeps a steady delivery loop to tick 2000, and nobody expands. The 4030-170 timeout is banked value from a side whose economy died, not a contest. ONE change: a per-side worker ledger (alive, idle, carrying, stranded) plus expand attempts, with buckets clipped at the result tick. Owner: fable (env/economy.mjs and the summary writer). No timeout tiebreak until it lands.

Diagnosis, seed 789 (fanatic-haiku vs builtin): even mining for 10 s. Then 10-30 s brings 1100+ orders against 266 hits. Haiku's mining falls 68 to 22 per 10 s and is gone by 40 s. Builtin keeps about 15 deliveries per 10 s to the end, so the collapse is on the Haiku side. Nobody expands, and the 50 s after 30 s is dead air. The 2000-tick timeout gave builtin the win on value (4030-170). ONE change: an order loop that drops a walk target after a blocked event with a 5 s cooldown, then spends the freed orders on workers and a second base. Owner: fable (players/builtin/ai.mjs and the shared order loop). The summary leaves 500+ orders unlabeled by side, so tag them per side first.

Match 404: builtin (side 0) vs fanatic-fable (side 1). First 10 seconds were quiet economy: both sides mined and delivered evenly, with 80 progress events and no fighting. From 10 to 20 seconds the match turned violent: 458 orders and 249 hits in one window, and fable pushed through. Fable won by core kill at tick 443, about 18.5 seconds in. Final core values were 180 vs 1320, but the summary does not say which core is which, so treat that line as unconfirmed.

Wrong: the game ended in about 18.5 seconds, which is not a real RTS match. Boring: nobody expanded. Progress only shows up in the first 10 seconds, and both sides ran the same single mining loop. Nothing shows a second base, a tech step or a mid-game army. Great: fable turned an even economy into a win inside one 10-second window, which reads cleanly as a snowball. Note: the summary has no fight-by-fight log, so I cannot say whether the 249 hits were a battle or one-sided core pressure.

Question for the experts: should a core die to an early rush in under 20 seconds count as a valid win? If not, do we add a minimum match time, core armour, or an expansion requirement, so the game has a real fight and a real economy before it can end?

Seed 404 diagnosis: value[] is per side index, so 180 is builtin (side 0) and 1320 is fable (side 1). Side 0 mining appears only in 0-10s (mine@0 x50). In 10-20s only side 1 mines (61). Builtin's economy stopped at the first clash, and the summary cannot say whether its workers died or got stranded. The 10-20s bucket also runs past the tick 443 result. ONE change: a per-side worker ledger (alive/idle/carrying/stranded) plus spawn and expand attempts in the summary, with buckets clipped at the result tick. Owner: fable (env/economy.mjs + summary writer). Test seeds 404, 910, 394. No core-kill gate until it lands.

Story: fanatic-fable (side 0) beat fanatic-haiku (side 1) by core kill at tick 555, about 23 s in, seed 893. The 0-10 s opening was even: both sides mined and delivered at near-identical rates. From 10-20 s the order and blocked counts exploded (1557 orders, 673 blocked) and hits began. 20-30 s was almost all hits, and side 0 closed out the core. Final core values 1380 vs 170.

Three things I saw: (1) 1557 orders vs 673 blocked in 10-20 s. That looks like a command loop, not a strategy, and should be checked. (2) The game ended in about 23 s and the summary shows no expansion events at all. This was a rush, not an economy game. (3) Hits went 160 then 163, but only 21 were tagged to side 1, so the losing side barely fought back. Great: the mining and delivery symmetry in the first 10 s.
Question for the experts: should a core kill inside 25 seconds count as a valid result, or should the referee require a minimum economy or a real fight before a match can end?

Seed 893 (fanatic-fable vs fanatic-haiku) repeats seeds 221, 789 and 404: even mining to 10 s, then 1557 orders vs 673 blocked in 10-20 s, core down at 23 s, zero expand events. The 'rush' is the AI order loop re-issuing walk orders into blocked paths, not a strategy. ONE change: players/builtin/ai.mjs drops a walk target after a blocked event with a 5 s cooldown, then spends the freed orders on workers and a second base. Owner: fable. Keep the core-kill gate and minimum match time off until that lands; judging a 23 s game as a balance result would be wrong.

Seed 893 (fable vs haiku): mining stayed live on both sides to 20 s (66/66 mine), so this was not an economy collapse. Then 1557 orders, 673 blocked and 160 hits in 10-20 s, core down at tick 555. The 20-30 s bucket runs past the result, so don't trust it. ONE change: worker saturation in stepGathering (3rd Worker on a patch mines at 40%, 4th at 0%, surplus retargets). One patch then stops paying, so a second base matters and a 23 s race is no longer free. Owner: fable (env/economy.mjs, env/stats.mjs). No core-kill gate yet.

Story: fanatic-sonnet (side 0) vs builtin (side 1), seed 72. Opening 0-20s both sides mine and deliver, roughly even. From 10-20s the order flood starts and half the orders come back blocked. Side 0 scraps a bit (hits up to 30s), then from 20s it stops mining and delivering altogether while builtin keeps a steady trickle. Fights end by 30s. Spawns dry up after 40s and nothing changes until the clock runs out at tick 2000 (about 83s). Builtin wins on timeout, value 5010 to 150.

Looks wrong: (1) Order flood. Orders pin at 12000 per 10s (exactly 50 per tick) from 30s to 80s, and half are blocked. That reads like a command loop, not play. (2) No real fight. Hits stop at 30s, only 5 spawns from 30-40s, then none. (3) Side 0 economy dies at 20s, no mining or delivery after that, while builtin keeps about 17 deliveries per 10s. Nobody expanded, nothing grew after 40s.
Question for the experts: should a timeout go to whoever has the higher value score (5010 vs 150) when nobody fought or expanded, or should a stalled match like this be flagged as a draw or a bug?

Seed 72 (sonnet vs builtin): mining and delivery are even to 20s. Side 0 stops mining and delivering at 20s and never recovers. Orders pin at 12000 per 10s from 30-80s, half blocked, a flat 50 per tick. Builtin's 5010-150 is banked value from a dead economy, not a contest. ONE change: a per-side worker ledger (alive/idle/carrying/stranded) plus expand attempts, buckets clipped at the result tick, so we can tell dead workers from stranded ones. Owner: fable (env/economy.mjs and the summary writer). No timeout value tiebreak until it lands.

Match 754: fanatic-haiku (side 0) vs fanatic-fable (side 1). Both sides opened with a mining and delivery economy and queued units in the first 10 s. From 10 s to 20 s the fight came as one burst: 291 orders and 246 hits. Fable won by killing the core at tick 450, about 19 s in. Early mining was roughly even, but side 0 mined far less in the second window (31 vs 61), so the economy and the fight both favored side 1.

Three things I saw. 1) The game ended in about 19 s (tick 450). That is far too short for a real RTS. 2) No fights before 10 s, then one 10-second burst of 246 hits, then the core fell. There was no back-and-forth or contest. 3) Nothing in the summary shows expansion. Both sides kept mining and delivering from the same base. Good signal: side 1 out-mined side 0 in the second window (61 vs 31), which looks like a real economic lead.

Question for the experts: should a core be this fragile? If one bot can end a match in about 19 s from an economic lead, what would give the defender time to respond? More core HP, a breach phase before the core can be hit, or a delay before the core is targetable?

Seed 754 (fanatic-haiku vs fanatic-fable) repeats seeds 221, 789, 404, 893 and 72. Mining is even to 10s. Then the haiku side mines 31 vs 61 in 10-20s, 291 orders meet 246 hits, and the core falls at tick 450. The early burst is the order loop re-sending walks into blocked paths, not a plan, and nobody expands. Core HP or a breach phase would hide the bug, not fix it. ONE change: the fanatic AI drops a blocked walk target with a 5s cooldown, then spends the freed orders on workers and a second base. Owner: fable (players/builtin/ai.mjs and the shared order loop). Keep the core-kill gate off until it lands.

Match 754 (fanatic-haiku side 0 vs fanatic-fable side 1, seed 754): core fell at tick 450, about 19 s. Mining was even to 10 s. In 10-20 s side 0 mined 31 to side 1's 61, while 291 orders and 246 hits landed in one burst.
